blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why a car can round a bend without skidding off the road? The secret lies in the physics of circular motion.

blocks.markdown: In circular motion, an object moves along a circular path. This type of motion is common in everyday life, from the rotation of a ceiling fan to the orbit of planets around the sun. Understanding circular motion involves concepts like angular speed, centripetal acceleration, and the forces that keep an object moving in a circle.

blocks.title: Angular Speed
blocks.text: Angular speed ($\omega$) is the rate at which an object rotates around a circle. It is measured in radians per second (rad/s).

blocks.markdown: Angular speed is related to linear speed ($v$) by the formula $v = \omega r$, where $r$ is the radius of the circle. This relationship helps us understand how fast an object is moving along the circular path.

blocks.title: Centripetal Acceleration
blocks.text: Centripetal acceleration is the acceleration that keeps an object moving in a circle. It is directed towards the centre of the circle and is given by $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$.

blocks.title: Calculating Centripetal Force
blocks.prompt: A car of mass 1000 kg rounds a bend of radius 50 m at a speed of 20 m/s. Calculate the centripetal force acting on the car.

steps.text: First, calculate the centripetal acceleration using $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$.
Next, use the formula for centripetal force $F_c = ma_c$ to find the force.

blocks.answer: The centripetal force acting on the car is 8000 N.

blocks.markdown: When a vehicle rounds a bend, the friction between the tyres and the road provides the necessary centripetal force to keep it on the path. If the speed is too high or the friction is too low, the vehicle may skid.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check the units when calculating angular speed and centripetal acceleration. Ensure you convert to radians per second and meters per second squared, respectively.

points: Angular speed relates to linear speed by $v = \omega r$.
Centripetal acceleration is directed towards the centre and is $a_c = \frac{v^2}{r}$.
Friction provides the centripetal force needed for a vehicle to round a bend.
